description: Aeons is passionate team on a mission to show just how much fun astronaut training can be. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are blending science, education, and space exploration into interactive games, detailed statistics, and dynamic animations. Our goal is to bring the wonders of planets, moons, and the cosmos straight to your screen!
summary: ASTRIVA: Mars Outpost Mission Simulator is a bilingual (English and Burmese) educational survival game for kids aged 7 to 12. Using real NASA Mars data, players train as Junior Astronauts by passing a space qualification exam, managing a 500 kg launch cargo budget, and surviving 30 days on Mars—balancing oxygen, water, food, and power while driving rovers, collecting 12 Martian minerals, and asking science questions to MARS-1 AI.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
ASTRIVA: Mars Outpost Mission Simulator is an interactive educational survival game designed for kids aged 7 to 12. Players train as Junior Astronauts across three phases:

  1. Qualification Exam: Players study real Mars facts (temperature, gravity, atmosphere, and radiation) and pass a cadet quiz.
  2. Launch Prep: Players balance crew size and supplies within a 500 kg weight budget before launching to Mars.
  3. 30-Day Mars Survival: Players survive for 30 Martian days (Sols) by managing oxygen, water, rations, and power. They can drive rovers, explore the habitat, farm crops, collect 12 real Martian minerals, build colony beacons, and ask science questions to an in-game assistant (MARS-1 AI).

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Space science can feel difficult or boring when learned only from textbooks. ASTRIVA makes learning fun and hands-on, helping young learners in Myanmar and around the world understand real space exploration challenges. It also supports both English and Burmese so local students can easily play and learn.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

  • Coding: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • Design & UI/UX: Figma, Canva
  • Hosting & Version Control: GitHub, GitHub Pages
  • Video & Audio: CapCut, Clideo
  • NASA Data: Facts and mineral data sourced from the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) and NASA's Mars rover missions.

Creativity & Factors Considered:
We focused on age-appropriate visuals, simple controls, bilingual accessibility (English and Burmese), and realistic survival trade-offs (like power vs. shielding during solar events) so kids learn critical thinking while having fun.
